bibliography.note: Crossref dates it 2016 (online first); the volume is 2017, 20(1): 98–111, as the paper has. The PDF's first page is the repository's cover sheet, so journal page = PDF page + 96 (p. 98 = PDF p. 2; findin's 'printed' labels on this file are off and should be ignored).

claims.claim: Under ice, phytoplankton biovolume averaged 15.8 % and chlorophyll 43.2 % of summer values across 101 lakes
claims.source_value: 43.2 % (chlorophyll a, 118 stations with paired winter–summer data) and 15.8 % (phytoplankton biovolume, only 17 stations) — means across the stations that had each variable, within a 101-lake data set
claims.location: p. 98 (PDF p. 2), Abstract; p. 101 (PDF p. 5), Methods (station counts); p. 102 (PDF p. 6) and p. 103 (PDF p. 7), Results
claims.quote: mean winter values were 43.2% of summer values for chlorophyll a, 15.8% of summer
claims.conditions: global synthesis, 42 research groups, data 1940–2015; ratio of mean winter to mean summer value (winter chl a 5.87 ± 0.88 against summer 13.6 ± 2.84 µg/L); 'phytoplankton biovolume averaged about 1/6th that of the summer average (n = 17)'
claims.note: The digits are right, but '101 lakes' is the size of the whole data set, not of these means: the biovolume figure rests on 17 stations and the chlorophyll figure on 118. Suggested wording: 'phytoplankton biovolume averaged 15.8 % (17 stations) and chlorophyll 43.2 % (118 stations) of summer values in a 101-lake synthesis'.

claims.claim: Under ice, crustacean density averaged 27.8 ind/L against 110 ind/L in summer across 36 stations
claims.location: p. 103 (PDF p. 7), Results; p. 104 (PDF p. 8), Table 1 (crustacean zooplankton density, 36 winter observations)
claims.quote: significantly lower under ice (27.8 ± 11.2 individuals L-1) than during summer (110 ± 30.8
claims.conditions: mean ± SE across 36 stations; crustacean zooplankton only (rotifers and 'other' zooplankton excluded because methods differed); individuals per litre

claims.claim: copepods made up about 80 % of winter and 63 % of summer crustacean density (shares read from a figure)
claims.quote: Average community composition for major phytoplankton and crustacean zooplankton groups during the winter and summer
claims.conditions: Fig. 3, proportion of total crustacean density averaged across stations; read off the bars: winter calanoids 0–0.28 + cyclopoids 0.28–0.80 (≈ 80 % copepods), summer calanoids 0–0.21 + cyclopoids 0.21–0.64 (≈ 63–64 %)
claims.note: Read from the bar chart, as the paper says; Daphnia ≈ 14 % of winter and ≈ 19 % of summer density, other cladocerans the rest.

claims.claim: field: under ice ~25 % of summer density, ~80 % of it copepods (Hampton et al. 2017)
claims.location: p. 98 (PDF p. 2), Abstract; p. 104 (PDF p. 8), Fig. 3
claims.quote: 15.8% of summer phytoplankton biovolume and 25.3% of summer zooplankton density
claims.conditions: crustacean zooplankton, individuals per litre, 36 stations; copepod share read from Fig. 3

claims.claim: Hampton et al. 2017: under ice ~25 % of the summer stock (of zooplankton)
claims.source_value: 25.3 % of summer crustacean zooplankton DENSITY (individuals per litre); no winter/summer biomass ratio is given
claims.note: The sim's zooplankton are biomass fields; a share by number is not a share by mass when winter stock is mostly copepods (smaller per individual than Daphnia). Say 'density' in the comment.

notes: Useful beyond the cited values: winter TDN ≈ 2× summer (707 vs 375 µg/L), and in the shallowest lakes (< 2.10 m) winter TDN was 2,070 µg/L higher than summer; chl a disparity greatest in lakes < 2.93 m deep (summer higher by 52.3 µg/L). Zooplankton density was lower in winter at 10 of 11 long-term sites. These are cross-lake averages dominated by deeper, often northern lakes; latitude is shown in Fig. 2.
